name: Isometric Hold (Pull-Up)
movementPattern: Isometric vertical pull - top position hold
grip: Overhand pronated or neutral grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
description: Hold the top flexed position of a pull-up with chin over the bar for time, building maximum isometric pulling strength and scapular depression endurance.
setup: Step onto a bench or plyo box beneath a sturdy pull-up bar.
Grasp the bar with an overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Step off or jump to bring your chin comfortably cleared above the bar level, elbows driven down and back.
Brace your core, cross ankles, and depress scapulae down away from your ears.
instructions: Hold the top flexed position statically, resisting gravity through intense muscular contraction of the lats and arm flexors.
Keep chest proud, chin above the bar, and shoulders actively packed down.
Breathe steadily in short, controlled breaths throughout the hold duration.
Lower yourself down under complete control when target hold duration is reached.
cues: Pack shoulders tight away from ears.
commonMistakes: Resting chin on the bar to cheat the hold.
Letting shoulders elevate into a passive neck crunch.
Dropping suddenly from the bar without controlling the descent.

logging.example: 30 seconds held at top: record 30 s duration.
logging.note: Record duration held in seconds with chin cleared over bar. If performed with added weight belt, record external load and duration.

variantNote: Static isometric contraction held at peak concentric range of a pull-up. Used to develop pull-up capacity, lock-off strength, and grip endurance.
reviewNotes: Illustration depicts hanging pull-up start in panel A and static chin-over-bar top flexed position in panel B.
